mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over two consecutive months indicates a strengthening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances when HOUST increases for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances when UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a contraction in supply, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when INDPRO declines by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% in a month signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when RSAFS increases by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same month, it signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200,000 and UNRATE decrease > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over two consecutive months signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when CPIAUCSL increases for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) remains stable (growth < 0.5% month-over-month), it signals strong economic growth without significant inflation, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 2% QoQ and CPIAUCSL growth < 0.5% MoM
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when both conditions are met.
